Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

0 # bat

A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` ## Customization ### Highlighting theme Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: ```bash bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt ``` Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: ```bash export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" ``` `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. ### Output style Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: ```bash bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt ``` Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. ### Decorations By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option: ```bash bat --decorations=always myfile.txt # always show decorations bat --decorations=never myfile.txt # never show decorations ``` ### Using a different pager `bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`. To use a different pager: ```bash export BAT_PAGER="less -RF" ``` ### Configuration file `bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path: ```bash bat --config-file ``` Generate a default configuration file: ```bash bat --generate-config-file ``` The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example: ```bash # Set the theme --theme="TwoDark" # Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header --style="numbers,changes,header" # Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files --map-syntax "*.ino:C++" ``` ## Command-line options For a full list of options, run: ```bash bat --help ``` ## Project goals `bat` tries to achieve the following goals: - Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting - Integrate with Git to show file modifications - Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat` - Offer a user-friendly command-line interface ## License Copyright (c) 2018-2025 bat-developers `bat` is made available under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option. See the LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT files for license details.

Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - 0 # bat

A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ```

A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` ## Customization ### Highlighting theme Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: ```bash bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt ``` Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: ```bash export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" ``` `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. ### Output style Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: ```bash bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt ``` Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. ### Decorations By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option: ```bash bat --decorations=always myfile.txt # always show decorations bat --decorations=never myfile.txt # never show decorations ``` ### Using a different pager `bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`. To use a different pager: ```bash export BAT_PAGER="less -RF" ``` ### Configuration file `bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path: ```bash bat --config-file ``` Generate a default configuration file: ```bash bat --generate-config-file ``` The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example: ```bash # Set the theme --theme="TwoDark" # Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header --style="numbers,changes,header" # Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files --map-syntax "*.ino:C++" ``` ## Command-line options For a full list of options, run: ```bash bat --help ``` ## Project goals `bat` tries to achieve the following goals: - Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting - Integrate with Git to show file modifications - Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat` - Offer a user-friendly command-line interface ## License Copyright (c) 2018-2025 bat-developers `bat` is made available under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option. def get_config_dir():
    if 'BAT_CONFIG_PATH' in os.environ:
        return None  # direct file
    config_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.config'))
    return os.path.join(config_home, 'bat')

def get_config_file():
    if 'BAT_CONFIG_PATH' in os.environ:
        return os.environ['BAT_CONFIG_PATH']
    config_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.config'))
    return os.path.join(config_home, 'bat', 'config')

def get_cache_dir():
    if 'BAT_CACHE_PATH' in os.environ:
        return os.environ['BAT_CACHE_PATH']
    cache_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CACHE_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.cache'))
    return os.path.join(cache_home, 'bat')

def format_file_size(size_bytes):
    """Format file size like bat does."""
    if size_bytes < 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes} B"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / 1024:.1f} KiB"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / (1024 * 1024):.1f} MiB"
    else:
        return f"{size_bytes / (1024 * 1024 * 1024):.1f} GiB"

    if 'BAT_CONFIG_PATH' in os.environ:
        return None  # direct file
    config_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.config'))
    return os.path.join(config_home, 'bat')

def get_config_file():
    if 'BAT_CONFIG_PATH' in os.environ:
        return os.environ['BAT_CONFIG_PATH']
    config_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.config'))
    return os.path.join(config_home, 'bat', 'config')

def get_cache_dir():
    if 'BAT_CACHE_PATH' in os.environ:
        return os.environ['BAT_CACHE_PATH']
    cache_home = os.environ.get('XDG_CACHE_HOME', os.path.expanduser('~/.cache'))
    return os.path.join(cache_home, 'bat')

def format_file_size(size_bytes):
    """Format file size like bat does."""
    if size_bytes < 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes} B"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / 1024:.1f} KiB"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / (1024 * 1024):.1f} MiB"
    else:
        return f"{size_bytes / (1024 * 1024 * 1024):.1f} GiB"

def format_file_size(size_bytes):
    if size_bytes < 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes} B"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / 1024:.1f} KiB"
    elif size_bytes < 1024 * 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{size_bytes / (1024 * 1024):.1f} MiB"
    else:

def detect_language_from_filename(filename, syntax_mappings=None):
    """Detect language from filename."""
    if syntax_mappings:
        basename = os.path.basename(filename)
        for pattern, lang in syntax_mappings:
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(basename, pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(filename, pattern):
                return lang

    basename = os.path.basename(filename)
    # Try exact name match first

    # Try extension match

        for name, exts_str in LANGUAGES:
            exts = exts_str.split(',')
            if ext in exts or f".{ext}" in exts:
                return name

    return None

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Output formatting
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

BOX_H = '─'   # horizontal
BOX_V = '│'   # vertical
BOX_TL = '┌'  # top-left
BOX_TR = '┐'  # top-right
BOX_BL = '└'  # bottom-left
BOX_BR = '┘'  # bottom-right
BOX_LM = '├'  # left-middle
BOX_RM = '┤'  # right-middle
BOX_TM = '┬'  # top-middle
BOX_BM = '┴'  # bottom-middle
BOX_CR = '┼'  # cross

def make_grid_line(gutter_width, term_width, sep_char):
    """Make a horizontal grid line."""
    content_width = term_width - gutter_width - 1
    return BOX_H * gutter_width + sep_char + BOX_H * content_width

def make_snip_line(gutter_width, term_width, has_grid):
    """Make a snip line (between non-adjacent ranges)."""
    if has_grid:
        # " ... │ ─ ─ ... 8< ─ ─ ..."
        content_width = term_width - gutter_width - 1 - 2  # -2 for "│ "
        snip_content = make_snip_content(content_width)
        return f" ...{BOX_H * (gutter_width - 4)}{BOX_V} {snip_content}"
    else:
        # " ...─ ─ ... 8< ─ ─ ─"
        return make_snip_full(gutter_width, term_width)

def make_snip_full(gutter_width, term_width):
    """Make snip line without grid."""
    total = term_width
    prefix = " ..."
    suffix_pattern = "─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─"
    scissors = " 8< "
    
    # Build: " ...─ ─ ─ ... 8< ─ ─ ─ ..."
    # Fill to total width
    remaining = total - len(prefix)
    
    # Place scissors in middle
    half = remaining // 2
    left = "─ " * (half // 2)
    right_width = remaining - len(left) - len(scissors)
    right = "─ " * (right_width // 2)
    
    line = prefix + left + scissors + right
    # Trim to exact width
    if len(line) > total:
        line = line[:total]
    elif len(line) < total:
        line = line + "─" * (total - len(line))
    
    return line

def make_snip_content(width):
    """Make the content portion of a snip line."""
    scissors = " 8< "
    half = (width - len(scissors)) // 2
    left = "─ " * (half // 2 + 1)
    right = "─ " * (half // 2)
    result = left[:half] + scissors + right
    if len(result) > width:
        result = result[:width]
    elif len(result) < width:
        result = result + "─" * (width - len(result))
    return result

def make_snip_line_v2(gutter_width, term_width, has_grid, has_numbers):
    """
    Make the snip line that appears between non-adjacent line ranges.
    
    Patterns observed (term_width=80):
    - numbers+grid: ' ... │ ' + content(72 chars) -> len=79
    - numbers only: ' ...' + content(76 chars) -> len=80  
    - grid only: full(80 chars) -> len=80
    - neither:   full(80 chars) -> len=80
    """
    if has_numbers and has_grid:
        # ' ... │ ' prefix + content
        prefix = ' ... \u2502 '  # ' ... │ '
        content_width = term_width - len(prefix)
        content = make_scissors_content(content_width)
        return prefix + content
    elif has_numbers:
        # ' ...' prefix + content (dashes start right after)
        prefix = ' ...'
        content_width = term_width - len(prefix)
        content = make_scissors_dashes(content_width)
        return prefix + content
    else:
        # Full width scissors
        return make_scissors_full(term_width)

def make_scissors_content(width):
    """Make scissors pattern for content area: '─ '*N + '8<' + ' ─'*M = width chars."""
    # 8< should be roughly centered
    half = (width - 2) // 2
    # left: '─ ' repeating
    left_count = half // 2
    left = '─ ' * left_count
    # right: ' ─' repeating  
    right_width = width - len(left) - 2
    right_count = right_width // 2
    right = ' ─' * right_count
    result = left + '8<' + right
    # Adjust to exact width
    if len(result) < width:
        result = result + '─' * (width - len(result))
    return result[:width]

def make_scissors_dashes(width):
    """Make scissors with leading dashes: '─ '*N + '8<' + ' ─'*M = width."""
    # Starts with '─ ' pattern
    half = (width - 2) // 2
    left_count = half // 2
    left = '─ ' * left_count
    right_width = width - len(left) - 2
    right_count = right_width // 2
    right = ' ─' * right_count
    result = left + '8<' + right
    if len(result) < width:
        result = result + '─' * (width - len(result))
    return result[:width]

def make_scissors_full(width):
    """Make full-width scissors: '─ '*N + '8<' + ' ─'*M = width."""
    # For no-numbers case, 8< ends up at position 38 (for width=80)

    right_count = right_width // 2
    right = ' ─' * right_count
    result = left + '8<' + right

def parse_config_file(config_path):
    """Parse bat config file and return list of args."""
    args = []
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                # Each line is a command-line argument
                args.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return args

    """Expand config args (might have quoted values)."""

    for arg in config_args:
        # Handle --key="value" or --key=value
        if '=' in arg and not arg.startswith('"'):
            expanded.append(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('"') and arg.endswith('"'):
            expanded.append(arg[1:-1])
        else:
            expanded.append(arg)
    return expanded

def parse_config_file(config_path):
    """Parse bat config file and return list of args."""
    args = []
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                # Each line is a command-line argument
                args.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return args

def expand_config_args(config_args):
    """Expand config args (might have quoted values)."""
    expanded = []
    for arg in config_args:
        # Handle --key="value" or --key=value
        if '=' in arg and not arg.startswith('"'):
            expanded.append(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('"') and arg.endswith('"'):
            expanded.append(arg[1:-1])
        else:
            expanded.append(arg)
    return expanded

    opts.strip_ansi = args.strip_ansi or 'never'
    opts.wrap_mode = args.wrap or 'auto'
    if args.chop_long_lines:
        opts.wrap_mode = 'never'
    opts.unbuffered = args.unbuffered
    
    # Terminal width
    tw = args.terminal_width
    opts.terminal_width = get_terminal_width(tw)
    
    # Paging
    paging = args.paging or 'auto'
    if args.paging_shortcut == 'never':
        paging = 'never'
    if hasattr(args, 'paging') and args.paging:
        paging = args.paging
    opts.paging = paging
    opts.pager = args.pager
    
    # Color detection
    stdout_is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
    color_when = args.color or 'auto'
    force_color = args.force_colorization
    
    if force_color:
        color_when = 'always'
    
    if color_when == 'always':
        opts.use_color = True
    elif color_when == 'never':
        opts.use_color = False
    else:  # auto
        opts.use_color = stdout_is_tty
    
    # Decorations
    deco_when = args.decorations or 'auto'
    if force_color:
        deco_when = 'always'
    
    # -p flag: plain mode
    if args.plain:
        if args.plain >= 2:
            deco_when = 'never'
            paging = 'never'
        else:
            deco_when = 'never'
    
    if deco_when == 'always':
        opts.use_decorations = True
    elif deco_when == 'never':
        opts.use_decorations = False
    else:  # auto
        opts.use_decorations = stdout_is_tty
    
    # Theme
    theme_env = os.environ.get('BAT_THEME', '')
    theme_dark_env = os.environ.get('BAT_THEME_DARK', '')
    theme_light_env = os.environ.get('BAT_THEME_LIGHT', '')
    
    theme = args.theme or theme_env or 'Monokai Extended'
    opts.theme = theme
    opts.theme_dark = args.theme_dark or theme_dark_env or 'Monokai Extended'
    opts.theme_light = args.theme_light or theme_light_env or 'Monokai Extended Light'
    
    # Style components
    style_env = os.environ.get('BAT_STYLE', '')
    style_str = args.style or style_env
    
    # Apply -n/--number shortcut
    if args.number:
        style_str = 'numbers'
    
    # Parse style
    if args.plain:
        style_components = set()
    elif style_str:
        style_components = parse_style(style_str)
        if style_components is None:
            style_components = set(DEFAULT_STYLE_COMPONENTS)
    else:
        style_components = set(DEFAULT_STYLE_COMPONENTS)
    
    # Only apply decorations if they should be shown
    if not opts.use_decorations:
        # In non-tty mode, don't show decorations unless style forces it
        # Actually, bat shows decorations based on the combination of
        # --decorations and --style flags
        # When decorations=auto and not tty: no decorations
        # But --number still works (it's an alias for --style=numbers)
        if args.number:
            # -n still shows numbers even in pipe mode
            style_components = {'numbers'}
            opts.use_decorations = True
        else:
            style_components = set()
    
    opts.show_numbers = 'numbers' in style_components
    opts.show_changes = 'changes' in style_components
    opts.show_grid = 'grid' in style_components
    opts.show_header_filename = 'header-filename' in style_components or 'header' in style_components
    opts.show_header_filesize = 'header-filesize' in style_components
    opts.show_snip = 'snip' in style_components
    opts.show_rule = 'rule' in style_components
    
    return opts

def main():
    # Build argument list: config args + env args + cli args
    config_file = get_config_file()
    config_args = []
    if os.path.exists(config_file):
        config_args = parse_config_file(config_file)
    
    env_args = parse_env_args()
    
    # Full args: config + env + sys.argv[1:]
    all_args = config_args + env_args + sys.argv[1:]
    
    parser = create_parser()
    
    # Handle unknown args gracefully
    try:
        args, unknown = parser.parse_known_args(all_args)
    except SystemExit:
        sys.exit(2)
    
    # Check for unknown arguments
    if unknown:
        # Filter out -- separator
        real_unknown = [u for u in unknown if u != '--']
        if real_unknown:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{real_unknown[0]}' found\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  tip: to pass '{real_unknown[0]}' as a value, use '-- {real_unknown[0]}'\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"Usage: bat [OPTIONS] [FILE]...\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"       bat <COMMAND>\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    
    # Handle --version
    if args.version:
        print(f"bat {VERSION} ({COMMIT})")
        return
    
    # Handle --help
    if args.help:
        # Check if -h or --help
        if '-h' in sys.argv and '--help' not in sys.argv:
            show_short_help()
        else:
            show_long_help()
        return
    
    # Handle --config-file
    if args.config_file:
        print(get_config_file())
        return
    
    # Handle --cache-dir
    if args.cache_dir:
        print(get_cache_dir())
        return
    
    # Handle --generate-config-file
    if args.generate_config_file:
        config_path = get_config_file()
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(config_path), exist_ok=True)
        config_content = """# This is `bat`s configuration file. Each line either contains a comment or
# a command-line option that you want to pass to `bat` by default. You can
# run `bat --help` to get a list of all possible configuration options.

# Specify desired highlighting theme (e.g. "TwoDark"). Run `bat --list-themes`
# for a list of all available themes
#--theme="TwoDark"

# Enable this to use italic text on the terminal. This is not supported on all
# terminal emulators (like tmux, by default):
#--italic-text=always

# Uncomment the following line to disable automatic paging:
#--paging=never

# Uncomment the following line if you are using less version >= 551 and want to
# enable mouse scrolling support in `bat` when running inside tmux. This might
# disable text selection, unless you press shift.
#--pager="less --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS --quit-if-one-screen --mouse"

# Syntax mappings: map a certain filename pattern to a language.
#   Example 1: use the C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files
#   Example 2: Use ".gitignore"-style highlighting for ".ignore" files
#--map-syntax "*.ino:C++"
#--map-syntax ".ignore:Git Ignore"
"""
        with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write(config_content)
        print(f"Success! Config file written to {config_path}")
        return
    
    # Handle --list-themes
    if args.list_themes:
        for theme in THEMES:
            print(theme)
        return
    
    # Handle --list-languages
    if args.list_languages:
        for name, exts in LANGUAGES:
            print(f"{name}:{exts}")
        return
    
    # Handle --diagnostic
    if args.diagnostic:
        show_diagnostic(args)
        return
    
    # Handle --acknowledgements
    if args.acknowledgements:
        show_acknowledgements()
        return
    
    # Handle --completion
    if args.completion:
        shell = args.completion
        comp_file = f'/workspace/completions/bat.{shell if shell != "ps1" else "ps1"}'
        if shell == 'bash':
            comp_file = '/workspace/completions/bat.bash'
        elif shell == 'fish':
            comp_file = '/workspace/completions/bat.fish'
        elif shell == 'zsh':
            comp_file = '/workspace/completions/bat.zsh'
        elif shell == 'ps1':
            comp_file = '/workspace/completions/bat.ps1'
        try:
            with open(comp_file) as f:
                sys.stdout.write(f.read())
        except:
            pass
        return
    
    # Handle cache subcommand
    if args.subcommand == 'cache':
        handle_cache(args)
        return
    
    # Build options
    opts = build_opts(args)
    
    # Create renderer
    renderer = BatRenderer(opts)
    
    # Determine files to process
    files = opts.files
    if not files:
        files = ['-']  # stdin
    
    # Handle -E quiet empty with stdin
    if opts.quiet_empty and files == ['-']:
        # Check if stdin is empty
        if sys.stdin.isatty():
            return  # No stdin data
    
    exit_code = 0
    total_files = len(files)
    
    for file_idx, filepath in enumerate(files):
        is_first = file_idx == 0
        is_last = file_idx == total_lines_count - 1 if False else (file_idx == total_files - 1)
        
        display_name = None
        if opts.file_names and file_idx < len(opts.file_names):
            display_name = opts.file_names[file_idx]
        
        is_stdin = filepath == '-'
        
        if is_stdin:
            # Read from stdin
            try:
                content_bytes = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            except:
                content_bytes = b''
            
            if opts.quiet_empty and not content_bytes:
                continue
            
            git_changes = None
            file_size = None
            
            process_file(
                filepath=None,
                content_bytes=content_bytes,
                opts=opts,
                renderer=renderer,
                is_first_file=is_first,
                is_last_file=is_last,
                display_name=display_name,
                file_size=None,
                is_stdin=True,
                git_changes=git_changes,
            )
        else:
            # Read from file
            if not os.path.exists(filepath):
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            
            if os.path.isdir(filepath):
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}' is a directory.")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            
            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(filepath)
                with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                    content_bytes = f.read()
            except PermissionError:
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': Permission denied (os error 13)")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            except OSError as e:
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            
            if opts.quiet_empty and not content_bytes:
                continue
            
            # Get git changes if needed
            git_changes = None
            if opts.show_changes or opts.diff:
                git_changes = get_git_changes(filepath)
            
            fn = display_name or os.path.basename(filepath)
            
            process_file(
                filepath=filepath,
                content_bytes=content_bytes,
                opts=opts,
                renderer=renderer,
                is_first_file=is_first,
                is_last_file=is_last,
                display_name=display_name or filepath,
                file_size=file_size,
                is_stdin=False,
                git_changes=git_changes,
            )
    
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def handle_cache(args):
    """Handle the cache subcommand."""
    if hasattr(args, 'help') and args.help:
        print("""Modify the syntax-definition and theme cache

Usage: executable cache [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -b, --build
          Initialize (or update) the syntax/theme cache by loading from the source directory
          (default: the configuration directory).

  -c, --clear
          Remove the cached syntax definitions and themes.

      --source <dir>
          Use a different directory to load syntaxes and themes from.

      --target <dir>
          Use a different directory to store the cached syntax and theme set.""")
        return
    
    if args.clear:
        cache_dir = get_cache_dir()
        for item in ['themes.bin', 'syntaxes.bin']:
            path = os.path.join(cache_dir, item)
            if os.path.exists(path):
                os.remove(path)
                print(f"Clearing {item.split('.')[0]} set cache ... okay")
            else:
                print(f"Clearing {item.split('.')[0]} set cache ... skipped (not present)")
        # metadata
        meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, 'metadata.yaml')
        if os.path.exists(meta_path):
            os.remove(meta_path)
            print("Clearing metadata file ... okay")
        else:
            print("Clearing metadata file ... skipped (not present)")
        return
    
    if args.build:
        cache_dir = get_cache_dir()
        source_dir = args.source if args.source else get_config_file().replace('/config', '')
        themes_dir = os.path.join(source_dir, 'themes')
        syntaxes_dir = os.path.join(source_dir, 'syntaxes')
        
        if not os.path.exists(themes_dir) or not os.listdir(themes_dir):
            print(f"No themes were found in '{themes_dir}', using the default set")
        
        if not os.path.exists(syntaxes_dir) or not os.listdir(syntaxes_dir):
            print(f"No syntaxes were found in '{syntaxes_dir}', using the default set.")
        
        os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
        
        # Create placeholder cache files
        target_dir = args.target if args.target else cache_dir
        themes_bin = os.path.join(target_dir, 'themes.bin')
        syntaxes_bin = os.path.join(target_dir, 'syntaxes.bin')
        
        with open(themes_bin, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(b'themes cache')
        print(f"Writing theme set to {themes_bin} ... okay")
        
        with open(syntaxes_bin, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(b'syntaxes cache')
        print(f"Writing syntax set to {syntaxes_bin} ... okay")
        
        meta_dir = target_dir
        print(f"Writing metadata to folder {meta_dir} ... okay")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

        if language:

def do_highlight(content, language, theme, filename=None):

    try:

        from pygments.lexers import TextLexer
        from pygments.util import ClassNotFound
        
        lexer = get_pygments_lexer(language, filename)
        if lexer is None:

            return None

        try:

            get_style_by_name(pygments_style)
        except:

        result = result.replace('\x1b[39m', '\x1b[0m')

            if r:

                if s is None:

                if e is None:
                    e = total_lines
                parsed_ranges.append((max(1, int(s)), min(total_lines, int(e))))

                else:
                    out.write(padding + '   ' + size_str + '\n')
            
            if has_grid and (has_header_fn or has_header_fs):
                # Middle grid separator
                mid = BOX_H * gutter_w + BOX_CR + BOX_H * (term_w - gutter_w - 1)
                out.write(colorf(mid, '38;5;246', use_color) + '\n')

                        out.write(colorf(sl, '38;5;246', use_color) + '\n')

                    continue

            if use_deco and has_snip and not prev_visible and not first_output:

                    parts.append(colorf('+', '32', use_color))
                elif change == 'modified':
                    parts.append(colorf('~', '33', use_color))
                else:
                    parts.append(' ')
                parts.append(' ')
            
            # Grid separator
            if use_deco and has_grid:
                parts.append(colorf(BOX_V, '38;5;246', use_color))
                parts.append(' ')
            
            # Content
            if hl_text is not None:

            elif use_color:

            else:

                gutter_taken = gutter_w + (2 if has_grid else 0)
                content_width = term_w - gutter_taken
                if vis_len < content_width:
                    content_part += f'\x1b[{bg}m' + ' ' * (content_width - vis_len)
                content_part += '\x1b[0m'
            
            parts.append(content_part)
            
            # Handle -n mode (numbers only, no decoration formatting needed for newline)
            line_out = ''.join(parts)
            
            # In number-only mode (non-tty), always add newline
            if use_deco or use_color:
                out.write(line_out + '\n')
            else:
                out.write(line_out)
                if ln < total_lines or has_final_nl:
                    out.write('\n')
        
        # Final snip (after last visible range)
        # Not needed - snip is between ranges
        
        # ── Bottom grid line ──
        if use_deco and has_grid:
            bot = BOX_H * gutter_w + BOX_BM + BOX_H * (term_w - gutter_w - 1)
            out.write(colorf(bot, '38;5;246', use_color) + '\n')
        
        # ── Rule between files ──
        if use_deco and has_rule and not is_last:
            rule = BOX_H * term_w
            out.write(colorf(rule, '38;5;246', use_color) + '\n')
    
    out.flush()

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Cache subcommand
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def handle_cache_cmd(args):
    i = 0
    do_build = False
    do_clear = False
    source_dir = None
    target_dir = None
    show_help = False
    
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a in ('-b', '--build'):
            do_build = True
        elif a in ('-c', '--clear'):
            do_clear = True
        elif a == '--source':
            i += 1
            source_dir = args[i] if i < len(args) else None
        elif a == '--target':
            i += 1
            target_dir = args[i] if i < len(args) else None
        elif a in ('-h', '--help'):
            show_help = True
        i += 1
    
    if show_help:
        sys.stdout.write("""Modify the syntax-definition and theme cache

Usage: executable cache [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -b, --build
          Initialize (or update) the syntax/theme cache by loading from the source directory
          (default: the configuration directory).

  -c, --clear
          Remove the cached syntax definitions and themes.

      --source <dir>
          Use a different directory to load syntaxes and themes from.

      --target <dir>
          Use a different directory to store the cached syntax and theme set.
""")
        return
    
    if do_clear:
        cache_dir = get_cache_dir()
        for name, fname in [('theme set', 'themes.bin'), ('syntax set', 'syntaxes.bin'), ('metadata file', None)]:
            if fname:
                path = os.path.join(cache_dir, fname)
                if os.path.exists(path):
                    os.remove(path)
                    print(f"Clearing {name} cache ... okay")
                else:
                    print(f"Clearing {name} cache ... skipped (not present)")
            else:
                meta_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, 'metadata.yaml')
                if os.path.exists(meta_path):
                    os.remove(meta_path)
                    print(f"Clearing {name} ... okay")
                else:
                    print(f"Clearing {name} ... skipped (not present)")
    
    if do_build:
        cache_dir = get_cache_dir()
        config_dir = os.path.dirname(get_config_file())
        src = source_dir or config_dir
        themes_src = os.path.join(src, 'themes')
        syntaxes_src = os.path.join(src, 'syntaxes')
        
        if not os.path.exists(themes_src) or not os.listdir(themes_src) if os.path.exists(themes_src) else True:
            print(f"No themes were found in '{themes_src}', using the default set")
        
        if not os.path.exists(syntaxes_src) or not os.listdir(syntaxes_src) if os.path.exists(syntaxes_src) else True:
            print(f"No syntaxes were found in '{syntaxes_src}', using the default set.")
        
        tgt = target_dir or cache_dir
        os.makedirs(tgt, exist_ok=True)
        
        themes_bin = os.path.join(tgt, 'themes.bin')
        syntaxes_bin = os.path.join(tgt, 'syntaxes.bin')
        
        with open(themes_bin, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(b'bat themes cache placeholder')
        print(f"Writing theme set to {themes_bin} ... okay")
        
        with open(syntaxes_bin, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(b'bat syntaxes cache placeholder')
        print(f"Writing syntax set to {syntaxes_bin} ... okay")
        
        print(f"Writing metadata to folder {tgt} ... okay")

# Main entry point
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

CONFIG_TEMPLATE = """# This is `bat`s configuration file. Each line either contains a comment or
# a command-line option that you want to pass to `bat` by default. You can
# run `bat --help` to get a list of all possible configuration options.

# Specify desired highlighting theme (e.g. "TwoDark"). Run `bat --list-themes`
# for a list of all available themes
#--theme="TwoDark"

# Enable this to use italic text on the terminal. This is not supported on all
# terminal emulators (like tmux, by default):
#--italic-text=always

# Uncomment the following line to disable automatic paging:
#--paging=never

# Uncomment the following line if you are using less version >= 551 and want to
# enable mouse scrolling support in `bat` when running inside tmux. This might
# disable text selection, unless you press shift.
#--pager="less --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS --quit-if-one-screen --mouse"

# Syntax mappings: map a certain filename pattern to a language.
#   Example 1: use the C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files
#   Example 2: Use ".gitignore"-style highlighting for ".ignore" files
#--map-syntax "*.ino:C++"
#--map-syntax ".ignore:Git Ignore"
"""

def read_config_file(path):
    """Read config file and return list of args."""
    args = []
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                args.append(line)
    except:
        pass
    return args

def main():
    # Build full arg list: config + BAT_OPTS + cli
    config_file = get_config_file()
    config_args = read_config_file(config_file)
    
    bat_opts = os.environ.get('BAT_OPTS', '').strip()
    env_args = shlex.split(bat_opts) if bat_opts else []
    
    all_argv = config_args + env_args + sys.argv[1:]
    
    opts = parse_args(all_argv)
    
    # ── Handle subcommands ──
    if opts.subcommand == 'cache':
        handle_cache_cmd(opts.subcommand_args)
        return
    
    # ── Handle info flags ──
    if opts.version:
        print(f"bat {VERSION} ({COMMIT})")
        return
    
    if opts.help:
        sys.stdout.write(read_file('long_help.txt'))
        return
    
    if opts.short_help:
        sys.stdout.write(read_file('short_help.txt'))
        return

        sys.stdout.write(read_file('acknowledgements.txt'))
        return
    
    if opts.completion:
        shell = opts.completion
        ext = {'bash': 'bash', 'fish': 'fish', 'zsh': 'zsh', 'ps1': 'ps1'}.get(shell, shell)
        sys.stdout.write(read_file(f'bat.{ext}'))
        return
    
    # ── Determine output mode ──
    stdout_is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
    
    # Color
    color_when = opts.color
    if opts.force_color:
        color_when = 'always'
    use_color = (color_when == 'always') or (color_when == 'auto' and stdout_is_tty)
    
    # Decorations
    deco_when = opts.decorations
    if opts.force_color:
        deco_when = 'always'
    if opts.plain >= 1:
        deco_when = 'never'
    if opts.plain >= 2:
        opts.paging = 'never'
    
    use_deco = (deco_when == 'always') or (deco_when == 'auto' and stdout_is_tty)
    
    # Theme
    theme = opts.theme or os.environ.get('BAT_THEME', 'Monokai Extended')
    if not theme:
        theme = 'Monokai Extended'
    
    # Style
    style_env = os.environ.get('BAT_STYLE', '')
    style_str = opts.style or style_env
    
    # Determine effective style components
    if opts.plain >= 1:
        components = set()
    elif opts.number:
        components = {'numbers'}
        use_deco = True  # -n forces number display even in pipe
    elif style_str:
        base = parse_style(style_env) if style_env else set(DEFAULT_COMPONENTS)
        components = parse_style(style_str, base)
        if components is None:
            components = set(DEFAULT_COMPONENTS)
    else:
        components = set(DEFAULT_COMPONENTS)
    
    # If not using decorations, suppress component display
    if not use_deco:
        # In non-TTY mode, most components are hidden
        # EXCEPT when explicitly forced (--decorations=always, --force-colorization)
        # The --number/-n flag is special - it shows numbers even in non-tty
        if not opts.number:
            components = set()
            use_deco = False
    
    opts.use_color = use_color
    opts.use_decorations = use_deco
    opts.show_numbers = 'numbers' in components
    opts.show_changes = 'changes' in components
    opts.show_grid = 'grid' in components
    opts.show_header_filename = 'header-filename' in components or 'header' in components
    opts.show_header_filesize = 'header-filesize' in components
    opts.show_snip = 'snip' in components
    opts.show_rule = 'rule' in components
    opts.theme = theme
    opts.terminal_width = get_terminal_width(opts.terminal_width_arg)
    if opts.chop:
        opts.wrap = 'never'
    if not hasattr(opts, 'fallback_syntax'):
        opts.fallback_syntax = None
    if not hasattr(opts, 'map_syntax') or opts.map_syntax is None:
        opts.map_syntax = []
    
    # ── Collect files to process ──
    files = opts.files if opts.files else ['-']
    
    exit_code = 0
    files_data = []
    
    for file_idx, filepath in enumerate(files):
        fn_override = None
        if opts.file_names and file_idx < len(opts.file_names):
            fn_override = opts.file_names[file_idx]
        
        is_stdin = filepath == '-'
        
        if is_stdin:
            try:
                content_bytes = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            except:
                content_bytes = b''
            
            if opts.quiet_empty and not content_bytes:
                continue
            
            display_name = fn_override or 'STDIN'
            files_data.append((display_name, content_bytes, None, True, None))
        else:
            if not os.path.exists(filepath):
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            if os.path.isdir(filepath):
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}' is a directory.")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(filepath)
                with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                    content_bytes = f.read()
            except PermissionError:
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': Permission denied (os error 13)")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            except OSError as e:
                bat_error(f"'{filepath}': {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})")
                exit_code = 1
                continue
            
            if opts.quiet_empty and not content_bytes:
                continue
            
            git_changes = None
            if opts.show_changes or opts.diff:
                git_changes = get_git_changes(filepath)
            
            display_name = fn_override or filepath
            files_data.append((display_name, content_bytes, file_size, False, git_changes))
    
    if not files_data:
        sys.exit(exit_code)
    
    render_output(opts, files_data)
    sys.exit(exit_code)
